content:
Four members of a family-run criminal enterprise were sentenced to state prison on November 4, 2026, for operating massage businesses in Ventura County, California, as fronts for commercial sex and laundering the proceeds for more than a decade, the Ventura County District Attorney's Office announced.

Xiangwei Ma, 56, identified by prosecutors as the head of the organization, was sentenced to 14 years and 8 months in state prison. Her brother Xiangdong Ma, 54, was sentenced to 10 years. Her sister Li Ma, 60, received 5 years and 4 months, and her husband Ming Ma received 4 years and 4 months. A jury convicted all four in September of pimping and money laundering; Xiangwei Ma was also convicted of mortgage fraud. A fifth defendant, Jaime Calderon, pleaded guilty to money laundering in August 2023 and received a county jail sentence.

According to the District Attorney's Office, the family operated storefronts including Miracle Massage in Ventura and A+ Massage in Port Hueneme, presenting them as legitimate massage businesses while investigators say they recruited and exploited women from China for commercial sex. The businesses operated for more than a decade.

Prosecutors say the family hid the proceeds through banks, life insurance policies, casinos and real estate deals, including a Simi Valley home bought through a straw buyer. The court ordered forfeiture of more than $1.25 million in seized currency, bank funds and life insurance cash values.

The investigation began in 2020 after several law enforcement agencies received anonymous letters reporting suspected prostitution and human trafficking at local massage parlors. Xiangwei Ma had previously pleaded guilty to attempted pandering in Los Angeles County and served an 18-month prison sentence; investigators say she resumed directing the businesses after her release while avoiding being listed as an owner or manager.

"Behind the doors of seemingly legitimate massage businesses in Ventura County was a criminal enterprise that exploited vulnerable women and generated enormous profits," Senior Deputy District Attorney Rikole Kelly said. "These convictions send a powerful message: our communities will not be a marketplace for commercial sex, and those who profit from exploiting others will be held accountable."

District Attorney Erik Nasarenko said the businesses were structured to survive even after arrests for pimping and prostitution, and that the money laundering investigation allowed investigators to seize the assets and shut the businesses down for good. The four will be transferred to the custody of the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation to begin serving their prison terms.

Sources: Ventura County District Attorney's Office; FOX 11 Los Angeles; Ventura County Star; KTLA 5 News

title: Four in Ma family sentenced to prison for massage-parlor sex and money-laundering operation
